Minecraft development and software tools

My development projects cover several different environments: a Minecraft client, a Paper server, Axiom’s tool interface, a browser and generated desktop UI code. Choosing the right environment is part of choosing the right tool.

Client and server are different deployment targets

HomeGUI runs in a Fabric client and reads home-command responses. TraceBTE runs on a Paper server and guides players through a tutorial. Neither is installed in the other’s directory, and a client interface does not override server permissions.

Railway Tools has another dependency boundary: it extends Axiom, which must be installed separately. The mods, plugins and addons guide compares these cases.

Web and software interfaces

The BTE calculator provides a browser interface for exploring projection scale. PineappleUI experiments with mapping HTML/CSS-like layouts to Java Swing, keeping its current target separate from planned frameworks.

Check requirements before installation

Minecraft versions, mod loaders, server APIs and permission systems are not interchangeable. Every project page records the reviewed documentation and links to the maintained source. For compatibility changes or bugs, use that repository’s issue tracker rather than relying on an old portfolio summary.
